# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1608 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1608 - **Title**: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1606` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1105 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:30:53Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T00:21:47Z ## PR Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1608._

> ℹ️ **10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the Flutter app host never installs the Copilot CLI identity — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`**

This install covers only the CLI host. The desktop/mobile app is a second first-class PAT surface: `fa_ui`'s connect sheet accepts pasted tokens (`copilot_connect_sheet.dart`, `copilotPasteTokenLabel`), and its chat runtime reaches the same PAT-mode headers through the harness (`AgentService._streamFunctionFor` → `providerStreamFunction('copilot')` → `streamCopilot`). Nothing under `flutter_app/` calls `installCopilotCliIdentity`, so app-originated PAT-mode requests send:

```
user-agent: copilot/fa (unknown) term/unknown
```

instead of `copilot/<version> (<os>) term/unknown`. The `fa` default keeps requests *working* by design, but whether the Copilot API tolerates a foreign version/OS in PAT mode is exactly what the ticket's live evidence pinned (and AC2's live smoke did not run). Two cheap options:

1. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity(version: …, os: …)` once at app boot (the barrel already exports it; `Platform.operatingSystem` is fine on IO hosts), or
2. verify the app path against a real seat and document that the CLI is the only host with the exact CLI-shaped UA.

Note the app *model fetch* is already correct — `fetchModelsForEndpoint` handles the PAT branch — this is only about the UA/OS slots.

---

### Thread 2 — `docs/agents/cli.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `/provider export` is missing from the in-REPL help**

The new command is documented here and in README/providers.md, but `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` was not updated:

- the `/provider` usage block (`... | chatgpt oauth [headless] | /provider copilot | codemie sso [orgUrl] | dial setup | kimi`) lists every sibling subcommand — `export` is absent;
- the `/provider copilot` paragraph below it still describes only "device flow … or by pasting an existing GitHub token" with no mention of PAT mode (fine-grained PAT used directly, no exchange).

A user in the REPL discovers `/provider export` only by reading the docs site. Please add `| /provider export` to the usage line and one or two sentences to the copilot paragraph (PAT mode + export), matching the tone of the neighboring entries.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the conversion drops the only CLI-level coverage of the OAuth dead-exchange arm**

This test used to be the only CLI-level check of the OAuth branch in `_applyCopilotCredentials` (dead exchange → `warning: ${error.message}` + `continuing — pick or type the model id manually`). Converting it to the PAT variant (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat` skips the pre-validation exchange entirely) leaves that `try fetchCopilotApiToken / on CopilotAuthException` arm untested at the connect-flow level — the provider-level 404/401 tests in `test/providers/copilot_test.dart` don't cover the CLI's warning print, and `_CopilotDialect`'s silent-empty behavior means a regression there would again drop users into manual model entry with no hint.

Cheap fix: keep this PAT test and add a sibling with an OAuth-shaped token (`gho_…`) + a 404 exchange mock asserting `contains('token exchange')` — the original skeleton, three lines different.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_effectivePlatform` is a byte-identical duplicate of the reader's helper**

Same function, same doc-comment shape, same `platform`-pin-else-`Platform` semantics as `clipboard_reader.dart` (gh-1575). Two copies will drift (e.g. someone adds a Fuchsia/`null` arm to one). A tiny shared `pasteboard_platform.dart` (or an exported helper from `paste_image.dart`, which both already import) would serve both sides and keep the conditional-import pattern symmetric.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1606 PAT mode lands clean: the token source short-circuits fine-grained PATs (no exchange, no cache, no doomed refresh-retry), request headers dispatch by token shape (vscode-chat for exchanged tokens, copilot-developer-cli for PATs), the OAuth device-flow path is byte-for-byte untouched, and the exported token never touches argv or the transcript. 73 scoped tests pass and `dart analyze lib bin test` is clean. No blocking findings.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `/provider export` missing from the in-REPL help (`cli_help.dart` usage block + copilot paragraph)
- ⚠️ the Flutter-app host never calls `installCopilotCliIdentity` — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`
- 💡 lost OAuth-arm CLI test, duplicated `_effectivePlatform`, unbounded clipboard subprocess, over-specific empty-models message
- AC2 (live Copilot-seat smoke) unverified — disclosed by the author

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `export` to the `/provider` usage block in `lib/src/cli_help.dart` (+ one PAT-mode sentence in the copilot paragraph) — the new command is invisible in-REPL
2. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity` at Flutter-app boot — app-side PAT requests currently present `copilot/fa (unknown)` instead of the documented CLI-shaped UA
3. AC2 (live smoke vs a real Copilot seat) remains unverified — honestly disclosed by the author; confirm before relying on PAT mode in production
4. Suggestions: restore the OAuth-arm CLI test, share `_effectivePlatform` with the reader, bound the clipboard subprocess, soften the empty-models message

---

# pr-1608: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless ## Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1608 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1608 - **Title**: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1606` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1105 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:30:53Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T00:21:47Z ## PR Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1608._

> ℹ️ **10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the Flutter app host never installs the Copilot CLI identity — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`**

This install covers only the CLI host. The desktop/mobile app is a second first-class PAT surface: `fa_ui`'s connect sheet accepts pasted tokens (`copilot_connect_sheet.dart`, `copilotPasteTokenLabel`), and its chat runtime reaches the same PAT-mode headers through the harness (`AgentService._streamFunctionFor` → `providerStreamFunction('copilot')` → `streamCopilot`). Nothing under `flutter_app/` calls `installCopilotCliIdentity`, so app-originated PAT-mode requests send:

```
user-agent: copilot/fa (unknown) term/unknown
```

instead of `copilot/<version> (<os>) term/unknown`. The `fa` default keeps requests *working* by design, but whether the Copilot API tolerates a foreign version/OS in PAT mode is exactly what the ticket's live evidence pinned (and AC2's live smoke did not run). Two cheap options:

1. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity(version: …, os: …)` once at app boot (the barrel already exports it; `Platform.operatingSystem` is fine on IO hosts), or
2. verify the app path against a real seat and document that the CLI is the only host with the exact CLI-shaped UA.

Note the app *model fetch* is already correct — `fetchModelsForEndpoint` handles the PAT branch — this is only about the UA/OS slots.

---

### Thread 2 — `docs/agents/cli.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `/provider export` is missing from the in-REPL help**

The new command is documented here and in README/providers.md, but `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` was not updated:

- the `/provider` usage block (`... | chatgpt oauth [headless] | /provider copilot | codemie sso [orgUrl] | dial setup | kimi`) lists every sibling subcommand — `export` is absent;
- the `/provider copilot` paragraph below it still describes only "device flow … or by pasting an existing GitHub token" with no mention of PAT mode (fine-grained PAT used directly, no exchange).

A user in the REPL discovers `/provider export` only by reading the docs site. Please add `| /provider export` to the usage line and one or two sentences to the copilot paragraph (PAT mode + export), matching the tone of the neighboring entries.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the conversion drops the only CLI-level coverage of the OAuth dead-exchange arm**

This test used to be the only CLI-level check of the OAuth branch in `_applyCopilotCredentials` (dead exchange → `warning: ${error.message}` + `continuing — pick or type the model id manually`). Converting it to the PAT variant (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat` skips the pre-validation exchange entirely) leaves that `try fetchCopilotApiToken / on CopilotAuthException` arm untested at the connect-flow level — the provider-level 404/401 tests in `test/providers/copilot_test.dart` don't cover the CLI's warning print, and `_CopilotDialect`'s silent-empty behavior means a regression there would again drop users into manual model entry with no hint.

Cheap fix: keep this PAT test and add a sibling with an OAuth-shaped token (`gho_…`) + a 404 exchange mock asserting `contains('token exchange')` — the original skeleton, three lines different.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_effectivePlatform` is a byte-identical duplicate of the reader's helper**

Same function, same doc-comment shape, same `platform`-pin-else-`Platform` semantics as `clipboard_reader.dart` (gh-1575). Two copies will drift (e.g. someone adds a Fuchsia/`null` arm to one). A tiny shared `pasteboard_platform.dart` (or an exported helper from `paste_image.dart`, which both already import) would serve both sides and keep the conditional-import pattern symmetric.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1606 PAT mode lands clean: the token source short-circuits fine-grained PATs (no exchange, no cache, no doomed refresh-retry), request headers dispatch by token shape (vscode-chat for exchanged tokens, copilot-developer-cli for PATs), the OAuth device-flow path is byte-for-byte untouched, and the exported token never touches argv or the transcript. 73 scoped tests pass and `dart analyze lib bin test` is clean. No blocking findings.

- ⚠️ `/provider export` missing from the in-REPL help (`cli_help.dart` usage block + copilot paragraph)

2. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity` at Flutter-app boot — app-side PAT requests currently present `copilot/fa (unknown)` instead of the documented CLI-shaped UA
3. AC2 (live smoke vs a real Copilot seat) remains unverified — honestly disclosed by the author; confirm before relying on PAT mode in production

# pr-1608: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless ## Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1608 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1608 - **Title**: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1606` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1105 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:30:53Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T00:21:47Z ## PR Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1608._

> ℹ️ **10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the Flutter app host never installs the Copilot CLI identity — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`**

This install covers only the CLI host. The desktop/mobile app is a second first-class PAT surface: `fa_ui`'s connect sheet accepts pasted tokens (`copilot_connect_sheet.dart`, `copilotPasteTokenLabel`), and its chat runtime reaches the same PAT-mode headers through the harness (`AgentService._streamFunctionFor` → `providerStreamFunction('copilot')` → `streamCopilot`). Nothing under `flutter_app/` calls `installCopilotCliIdentity`, so app-originated PAT-mode requests send:

```
user-agent: copilot/fa (unknown) term/unknown
```

instead of `copilot/<version> (<os>) term/unknown`. The `fa` default keeps requests *working* by design, but whether the Copilot API tolerates a foreign version/OS in PAT mode is exactly what the ticket's live evidence pinned (and AC2's live smoke did not run). Two cheap options:

1. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity(version: …, os: …)` once at app boot (the barrel already exports it; `Platform.operatingSystem` is fine on IO hosts), or
2. verify the app path against a real seat and document that the CLI is the only host with the exact CLI-shaped UA.

Note the app *model fetch* is already correct — `fetchModelsForEndpoint` handles the PAT branch — this is only about the UA/OS slots.

---

### Thread 2 — `docs/agents/cli.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `/provider export` is missing from the in-REPL help**

The new command is documented here and in README/providers.md, but `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` was not updated:

- the `/provider` usage block (`... | chatgpt oauth [headless] | /provider copilot | codemie sso [orgUrl] | dial setup | kimi`) lists every sibling subcommand — `export` is absent;
- the `/provider copilot` paragraph below it still describes only "device flow … or by pasting an existing GitHub token" with no mention of PAT mode (fine-grained PAT used directly, no exchange).

A user in the REPL discovers `/provider export` only by reading the docs site. Please add `| /provider export` to the usage line and one or two sentences to the copilot paragraph (PAT mode + export), matching the tone of the neighboring entries.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the conversion drops the only CLI-level coverage of the OAuth dead-exchange arm**

This test used to be the only CLI-level check of the OAuth branch in `_applyCopilotCredentials` (dead exchange → `warning: ${error.message}` + `continuing — pick or type the model id manually`). Converting it to the PAT variant (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat` skips the pre-validation exchange entirely) leaves that `try fetchCopilotApiToken / on CopilotAuthException` arm untested at the connect-flow level — the provider-level 404/401 tests in `test/providers/copilot_test.dart` don't cover the CLI's warning print, and `_CopilotDialect`'s silent-empty behavior means a regression there would again drop users into manual model entry with no hint.

Cheap fix: keep this PAT test and add a sibling with an OAuth-shaped token (`gho_…`) + a 404 exchange mock asserting `contains('token exchange')` — the original skeleton, three lines different.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_effectivePlatform` is a byte-identical duplicate of the reader's helper**

Same function, same doc-comment shape, same `platform`-pin-else-`Platform` semantics as `clipboard_reader.dart` (gh-1575). Two copies will drift (e.g. someone adds a Fuchsia/`null` arm to one). A tiny shared `pasteboard_platform.dart` (or an exported helper from `paste_image.dart`, which both already import) would serve both sides and keep the conditional-import pattern symmetric.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1606 PAT mode lands clean: the token source short-circuits fine-grained PATs (no exchange, no cache, no doomed refresh-retry), request headers dispatch by token shape (vscode-chat for exchanged tokens, copilot-developer-cli for PATs), the OAuth device-flow path is byte-for-byte untouched, and the exported token never touches argv or the transcript. 73 scoped tests pass and `dart analyze lib bin test` is clean. No blocking findings.

- ⚠️ `/provider export` missing from the in-REPL help (`cli_help.dart` usage block + copilot paragraph)

2. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity` at Flutter-app boot — app-side PAT requests currently present `copilot/fa (unknown)` instead of the documented CLI-shaped UA

# pr-1608: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless ## Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1608._

> ℹ️ **10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the Flutter app host never installs the Copilot CLI identity — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`**

This install covers only the CLI host. The desktop/mobile app is a second first-class PAT surface: `fa_ui`'s connect sheet accepts pasted tokens (`copilot_connect_sheet.dart`, `copilotPasteTokenLabel`), and its chat runtime reaches the same PAT-mode headers through the harness (`AgentService._streamFunctionFor` → `providerStreamFunction('copilot')` → `streamCopilot`). Nothing under `flutter_app/` calls `installCopilotCliIdentity`, so app-originated PAT-mode requests send:

```
user-agent: copilot/fa (unknown) term/unknown
```

instead of `copilot/<version> (<os>) term/unknown`. The `fa` default keeps requests *working* by design, but whether the Copilot API tolerates a foreign version/OS in PAT mode is exactly what the ticket's live evidence pinned (and AC2's live smoke did not run). Two cheap options:

1. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity(version: …, os: …)` once at app boot (the barrel already exports it; `Platform.operatingSystem` is fine on IO hosts), or
2. verify the app path against a real seat and document that the CLI is the only host with the exact CLI-shaped UA.

Note the app *model fetch* is already correct — `fetchModelsForEndpoint` handles the PAT branch — this is only about the UA/OS slots.

---

### Thread 2 — `docs/agents/cli.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `/provider export` is missing from the in-REPL help**

The new command is documented here and in README/providers.md, but `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` was not updated:

- the `/provider` usage block (`... | chatgpt oauth [headless] | /provider copilot | codemie sso [orgUrl] | dial setup | kimi`) lists every sibling subcommand — `export` is absent;
- the `/provider copilot` paragraph below it still describes only "device flow … or by pasting an existing GitHub token" with no mention of PAT mode (fine-grained PAT used directly, no exchange).

A user in the REPL discovers `/provider export` only by reading the docs site. Please add `| /provider export` to the usage line and one or two sentences to the copilot paragraph (PAT mode + export), matching the tone of the neighboring entries.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the conversion drops the only CLI-level coverage of the OAuth dead-exchange arm**

This test used to be the only CLI-level check of the OAuth branch in `_applyCopilotCredentials` (dead exchange → `warning: ${error.message}` + `continuing — pick or type the model id manually`). Converting it to the PAT variant (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat` skips the pre-validation exchange entirely) leaves that `try fetchCopilotApiToken / on CopilotAuthException` arm untested at the connect-flow level — the provider-level 404/401 tests in `test/providers/copilot_test.dart` don't cover the CLI's warning print, and `_CopilotDialect`'s silent-empty behavior means a regression there would again drop users into manual model entry with no hint.

Cheap fix: keep this PAT test and add a sibling with an OAuth-shaped token (`gho_…`) + a 404 exchange mock asserting `contains('token exchange')` — the original skeleton, three lines different.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_effectivePlatform` is a byte-identical duplicate of the reader's helper**

Same function, same doc-comment shape, same `platform`-pin-else-`Platform` semantics as `clipboard_reader.dart` (gh-1575). Two copies will drift (e.g. someone adds a Fuchsia/`null` arm to one). A tiny shared `pasteboard_platform.dart` (or an exported helper from `paste_image.dart`, which both already import) would serve both sides and keep the conditional-import pattern symmetric.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1606 PAT mode lands clean: the token source short-circuits fine-grained PATs (no exchange, no cache, no doomed refresh-retry), request headers dispatch by token shape (vscode-chat for exchanged tokens, copilot-developer-cli for PATs), the OAuth device-flow path is byte-for-byte untouched, and the exported token never touches argv or the transcript. 73 scoped tests pass and `dart analyze lib bin test` is clean. No blocking findings.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `/provider export` missing from the in-REPL help (`cli_help.dart` usage block + copilot paragraph)
- ⚠️ the Flutter-app host never calls `installCopilotCliIdentity` — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`
- 💡 lost OAuth-arm CLI test, duplicated `_effectivePlatform`, unbounded clipboard subprocess, over-specific empty-models message
- AC2 (live Copilot-seat smoke) unverified — disclosed by the author

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `export` to the `/provider` usage block in `lib/src/cli_help.dart` (+ one PAT-mode sentence in the copilot paragraph) — the new command is invisible in-REPL
2. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity` at Flutter-app boot — app-side PAT requests currently present `copilot/fa (unknown)` instead of the documented CLI-shaped UA
3. AC2 (live smoke vs a real Copilot seat) remains unverified — honestly disclosed by the author; confirm before relying on PAT mode in production
4. Suggestions: restore the OAuth-arm CLI test, share `_effectivePlatform` with the reader, bound the clipboard subprocess, soften the empty-models message

---

# pr-1608: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless ## Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1608 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1608 - **Title**: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1606` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1105 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T12:30:53Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-15T00:21:47Z ## PR Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1608._

> ℹ️ **10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the Flutter app host never installs the Copilot CLI identity — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`**

This install covers only the CLI host. The desktop/mobile app is a second first-class PAT surface: `fa_ui`'s connect sheet accepts pasted tokens (`copilot_connect_sheet.dart`, `copilotPasteTokenLabel`), and its chat runtime reaches the same PAT-mode headers through the harness (`AgentService._streamFunctionFor` → `providerStreamFunction('copilot')` → `streamCopilot`). Nothing under `flutter_app/` calls `installCopilotCliIdentity`, so app-originated PAT-mode requests send:

```
user-agent: copilot/fa (unknown) term/unknown
```

instead of `copilot/<version> (<os>) term/unknown`. The `fa` default keeps requests *working* by design, but whether the Copilot API tolerates a foreign version/OS in PAT mode is exactly what the ticket's live evidence pinned (and AC2's live smoke did not run). Two cheap options:

1. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity(version: …, os: …)` once at app boot (the barrel already exports it; `Platform.operatingSystem` is fine on IO hosts), or
2. verify the app path against a real seat and document that the CLI is the only host with the exact CLI-shaped UA.

Note the app *model fetch* is already correct — `fetchModelsForEndpoint` handles the PAT branch — this is only about the UA/OS slots.

---

### Thread 2 — `docs/agents/cli.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `/provider export` is missing from the in-REPL help**

The new command is documented here and in README/providers.md, but `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` was not updated:

- the `/provider` usage block (`... | chatgpt oauth [headless] | /provider copilot | codemie sso [orgUrl] | dial setup | kimi`) lists every sibling subcommand — `export` is absent;
- the `/provider copilot` paragraph below it still describes only "device flow … or by pasting an existing GitHub token" with no mention of PAT mode (fine-grained PAT used directly, no exchange).

A user in the REPL discovers `/provider export` only by reading the docs site. Please add `| /provider export` to the usage line and one or two sentences to the copilot paragraph (PAT mode + export), matching the tone of the neighboring entries.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the conversion drops the only CLI-level coverage of the OAuth dead-exchange arm**

This test used to be the only CLI-level check of the OAuth branch in `_applyCopilotCredentials` (dead exchange → `warning: ${error.message}` + `continuing — pick or type the model id manually`). Converting it to the PAT variant (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat` skips the pre-validation exchange entirely) leaves that `try fetchCopilotApiToken / on CopilotAuthException` arm untested at the connect-flow level — the provider-level 404/401 tests in `test/providers/copilot_test.dart` don't cover the CLI's warning print, and `_CopilotDialect`'s silent-empty behavior means a regression there would again drop users into manual model entry with no hint.

Cheap fix: keep this PAT test and add a sibling with an OAuth-shaped token (`gho_…`) + a 404 exchange mock asserting `contains('token exchange')` — the original skeleton, three lines different.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_effectivePlatform` is a byte-identical duplicate of the reader's helper**

Same function, same doc-comment shape, same `platform`-pin-else-`Platform` semantics as `clipboard_reader.dart` (gh-1575). Two copies will drift (e.g. someone adds a Fuchsia/`null` arm to one). A tiny shared `pasteboard_platform.dart` (or an exported helper from `paste_image.dart`, which both already import) would serve both sides and keep the conditional-import pattern symmetric.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1606 PAT mode lands clean: the token source short-circuits fine-grained PATs (no exchange, no cache, no doomed refresh-retry), request headers dispatch by token shape (vscode-chat for exchanged tokens, copilot-developer-cli for PATs), the OAuth device-flow path is byte-for-byte untouched, and the exported token never touches argv or the transcript. 73 scoped tests pass and `dart analyze lib bin test` is clean. No blocking findings.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `/provider export` missing from the in-REPL help (`cli_help.dart` usage block + copilot paragraph)
- ⚠️ the Flutter-app host never calls `installCopilotCliIdentity` — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`
- 💡 lost OAuth-arm CLI test, duplicated `_effectivePlatform`, unbounded clipboard subprocess, over-specific empty-models message
- AC2 (live Copilot-seat smoke) unverified — disclosed by the author

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `export` to the `/provider` usage block in `lib/src/cli_help.dart` (+ one PAT-mode sentence in the copilot paragraph) — the new command is invisible in-REPL
2. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity` at Flutter-app boot — app-side PAT requests currently present `copilot/fa (unknown)` instead of the documented CLI-shaped UA
3. AC2 (live smoke vs a real Copilot seat) remains unverified — honestly disclosed by the author; confirm before relying on PAT mode in production
4. Suggestions: restore the OAuth-arm CLI test, share `_effectivePlatform` with the reader, bound the clipboard subprocess, soften the empty-models message

# pr-1608: gh-1606 Copilot provider: support fine-grained PATs directly (skip exchange, send copilot-developer-cli identity headers) — enables COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN in headless ## Description Closes #1606 # gh-1606 — Copilot provider: fine-grained PAT support (PAT mode) + `/provider export` ### What changed - The `copilot` provider now accepts fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_…`) **directly**: when the GitHub credential is a PAT, the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange is skipped entirely and the raw PAT rides as the Bearer against the configured Copilot base URL (the seat's tier host — a PAT has no `proxy-ep` to learn a tenant host from), with the official Copilot CLI's first-party identity headers (`copilot-integration-id: copilot-developer-cli`, `user-agent: copilot/ () term/unknown`). This is the only request shape the Copilot API accepts a PAT with; `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN=github_pat_…` now works headless. - New `/provider export`: copies the saved Copilot account's full token to the clipboard (single account = no ceremony; several = the existing account picker; feedback is one line `token copied to clipboard`; the token never prints to the transcript). - Connect flow updated: the PAT paste hint explains direct-PAT mode (device flow stays recommended); a dead PAT surfaces at the model fetch ("no models for this PAT — check Copilot Requests permission/seat") instead of a forecast exchange 404. ### Key decisions - **PAT mode lives in the token source**: `CopilotTokenManager.get()` short-circuits PATs (no exchange, no cache, no refresh); `copilotRequestHeaders()` dispatches request headers by token shape — an exchanged token keeps the `vscode-chat` identity byte-for-byte, a PAT presents `copilot-developer-cli`. The 401/403 refresh-retry is skipped in PAT mode (nothing to refresh — no doomed retry). - The `/models` dialect gets the same split: PAT → `GET {configured-base}/models` with PAT headers; OAuth → existing exchange + `proxy-ep` derivation, untouched. - Version/OS for the user-agent are host-installed at startup (`installCopilotCliIdentity` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`) — `lib/` stays pure Dart. - Clipboard writes go through a new `clipboard_writer.dart` (pbcopy / xclip→wl-copy / clip; the token rides **stdin**, never argv) behind the same web-safe conditional-import pattern as the pasteboard reader, plus an `AgentCliConfig.clipboardWrite` test seam. - OAuth path unchanged: exchange, proactive ~30-min refresh, 401 refresh+retry all preserved (existing tests green). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/providers/copilot_test.dart # PAT mode group: no exchange, PAT bearer + identity headers, chat + /models dart test test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart test/cli/clipboard_writer_test.dart ``` Docs: `docs/agents/providers.md` (new "GitHub Copilot credentials" table — device flow recommended / `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` env as OAuth or fine-grained PAT / classic `ghp_` never supported), README Copilot section, CHANGELOG under Unreleased. **Not verified here**: the live smoke against a real Copilot Business seat (AC2) — this ephemeral CI runner holds no Copilot-seat credential; AC1's mocked-http tests cover the wire shape the smoke would check.
Request flow ```mermaid flowchart TD CRED[GitHub credential] -->|gho_/ghu_ OAuth| EX[POST copilot_internal/v2/token exchange] EX --> TOK[~30-min Copilot API token + proxy-ep host] CRED -->|github_pat_ PAT| PAT[raw PAT is the Bearer] TOK --> API[copilot API base URL] PAT --> API API --> HDR[vscode-chat identity · OAuth
copilot-developer-cli + copilot/<version> UA · PAT] HDR --> MODELS[GET /models] HDR --> CHAT[POST /chat/completions] ```

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1608._

> ℹ️ **10 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the Flutter app host never installs the Copilot CLI identity — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`**

This install covers only the CLI host. The desktop/mobile app is a second first-class PAT surface: `fa_ui`'s connect sheet accepts pasted tokens (`copilot_connect_sheet.dart`, `copilotPasteTokenLabel`), and its chat runtime reaches the same PAT-mode headers through the harness (`AgentService._streamFunctionFor` → `providerStreamFunction('copilot')` → `streamCopilot`). Nothing under `flutter_app/` calls `installCopilotCliIdentity`, so app-originated PAT-mode requests send:

```
user-agent: copilot/fa (unknown) term/unknown
```

instead of `copilot/<version> (<os>) term/unknown`. The `fa` default keeps requests *working* by design, but whether the Copilot API tolerates a foreign version/OS in PAT mode is exactly what the ticket's live evidence pinned (and AC2's live smoke did not run). Two cheap options:

1. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity(version: …, os: …)` once at app boot (the barrel already exports it; `Platform.operatingSystem` is fine on IO hosts), or
2. verify the app path against a real seat and document that the CLI is the only host with the exact CLI-shaped UA.

Note the app *model fetch* is already correct — `fetchModelsForEndpoint` handles the PAT branch — this is only about the UA/OS slots.

---

### Thread 2 — `docs/agents/cli.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `/provider export` is missing from the in-REPL help**

The new command is documented here and in README/providers.md, but `lib/src/cli/cli_help.dart` was not updated:

- the `/provider` usage block (`... | chatgpt oauth [headless] | /provider copilot | codemie sso [orgUrl] | dial setup | kimi`) lists every sibling subcommand — `export` is absent;
- the `/provider copilot` paragraph below it still describes only "device flow … or by pasting an existing GitHub token" with no mention of PAT mode (fine-grained PAT used directly, no exchange).

A user in the REPL discovers `/provider export` only by reading the docs site. Please add `| /provider export` to the usage line and one or two sentences to the copilot paragraph (PAT mode + export), matching the tone of the neighboring entries.

---

### Thread 3 — `test/cli/copilot_provider_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the conversion drops the only CLI-level coverage of the OAuth dead-exchange arm**

This test used to be the only CLI-level check of the OAuth branch in `_applyCopilotCredentials` (dead exchange → `warning: ${error.message}` + `continuing — pick or type the model id manually`). Converting it to the PAT variant (`isFineGrainedGitHubPat` skips the pre-validation exchange entirely) leaves that `try fetchCopilotApiToken / on CopilotAuthException` arm untested at the connect-flow level — the provider-level 404/401 tests in `test/providers/copilot_test.dart` don't cover the CLI's warning print, and `_CopilotDialect`'s silent-empty behavior means a regression there would again drop users into manual model entry with no hint.

Cheap fix: keep this PAT test and add a sibling with an OAuth-shaped token (`gho_…`) + a 404 exchange mock asserting `contains('token exchange')` — the original skeleton, three lines different.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `_effectivePlatform` is a byte-identical duplicate of the reader's helper**

Same function, same doc-comment shape, same `platform`-pin-else-`Platform` semantics as `clipboard_reader.dart` (gh-1575). Two copies will drift (e.g. someone adds a Fuchsia/`null` arm to one). A tiny shared `pasteboard_platform.dart` (or an exported helper from `paste_image.dart`, which both already import) would serve both sides and keep the conditional-import pattern symmetric.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/cli/clipboard_writer.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: no timeout on the clipboard subprocess — a wedged writer holds the flow gate shut**

`_runWithStdin` awaits the child process with no deadline. If a pasteboard binary hangs instead of exiting (a shadowed `pbcopy` script, `xclip` blocking on a dead `$DISPLAY`, a wedged `wl-copy`), this future never resolves — and `_handleProviderExportCommand` holds `_providerFlowActive = true` until it does, so every later `/provider …` flow silently no-ops until the process restarts (the gate has no timeout of its own).

A bounded `.timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))` mapped to `PasteboardWriteUnavailable('clipboard writer timed out')` caps the blast radius; the loop's `on Object` fallthrough already gives it a natural home (try the next path, then the named unavailable). The gh-1575 reader (`_runBinaryProcess`) shares the trait — same fix applies there.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the empty-models note conflates transport failures with permission/seat problems**

The note names two specific causes ("check the Copilot Requests permission … and the account's Copilot seat"), but `_CopilotDialect.fetch` collapses *every* failure into an empty list — 15s timeout, HTTP 5xx, TLS failure, malformed JSON all land here. A user with a perfectly good PAT and a flaky network gets sent token-hunting in GitHub settings.

Either soften the wording ("the Copilot API returned no models for this PAT — it was rejected, granted nothing, or the request failed; check the \"Copilot Requests\" permission and the Copilot seat"), or have the PAT branch distinguish a non-200 status from a thrown transport error before this note prints.

---

### Thread 14

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-15):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE (with suggestions)

**Summary**: gh-1606 PAT mode lands clean: the token source short-circuits fine-grained PATs (no exchange, no cache, no doomed refresh-retry), request headers dispatch by token shape (vscode-chat for exchanged tokens, copilot-developer-cli for PATs), the OAuth device-flow path is byte-for-byte untouched, and the exported token never touches argv or the transcript. 73 scoped tests pass and `dart analyze lib bin test` is clean. No blocking findings.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `/provider export` missing from the in-REPL help (`cli_help.dart` usage block + copilot paragraph)
- ⚠️ the Flutter-app host never calls `installCopilotCliIdentity` — app-side PAT requests present `copilot/fa (unknown)`
- 💡 lost OAuth-arm CLI test, duplicated `_effectivePlatform`, unbounded clipboard subprocess, over-specific empty-models message
- AC2 (live Copilot-seat smoke) unverified — disclosed by the author

**Next Steps**:
1. Add `export` to the `/provider` usage block in `lib/src/cli_help.dart` (+ one PAT-mode sentence in the copilot paragraph) — the new command is invisible in-REPL
2. Call `installCopilotCliIdentity` at Flutter-app boot — app-side PAT requests currently present `copilot/fa (unknown)` instead of the documented CLI-shaped UA
3. AC2 (live smoke vs a real Copilot seat) remains unverified — honestly disclosed by the author; confirm before relying on PAT mode in production
4. Suggestions: restore the OAuth-arm CLI test, share `_effectivePlatform` with the reader, bound the clipboard subprocess, soften the empty-models message
